milestone.name: M1-M3 — full origination-to-repayment lifecycle (all three PRD milestones in one graph)

decisions.question: How much of the PRD's build order should this /spec run expand into the story graph?
decisions.chosen: All 3 milestones in one graph, epics tagged M1/M2/M3 so /auto ratchets in PRD order
decisions.rationale: Total capstone scope is fixed by the 29 adopted requirements and bounded by 10 safeguards, so there is no scope discovery left for a later run to do. Deferring M2/M3 would buy a second full /spec-to-/design cycle for no new information, and M3's disburse-and-repay done_when is part of the graded deliverable.

decisions.question: How finely should the 29 requirements be cut into epics?
options: Coarse — 10 epics merged by actor and lifecycle stage
decisions.chosen: Fine — 17 epics, each owning 1-2 requirements (see epic_catalog)
decisions.rationale: One-to-two requirements per epic gives each story group a disjoint file-ownership set, which is what lets /auto fan out parallel implementer teammates without write contention. Coarse epics would put Intake, Scoring and Decision in one owned tree.

decisions.question: Risk R-4: no requirement fixes the delinquency day ranges, and AC-09 pins 35 days past due to DPD-30. Which bucket ladder?
options: Four buckets plus an orthogonal NPA flag at 90 DPD
decisions.chosen: Floor semantics: CURRENT 0-29, DPD-30 30-59, DPD-60 60-89, DPD-90 90-179, NPA >=180 days past due, computed from the oldest unpaid installment's due date
decisions.rationale: AC-09 requires 35 DPD to read as DPD-30, which rules out 1-30/31-60 band semantics. Floors keep all five FR-09 buckets non-empty and mutually exclusive, and placing NPA at 180 avoids collapsing DPD-90 and NPA into the same range. The four-buckets-plus-flag option contradicts FR-09, which lists NPA as one of five buckets.

decisions.question: Risk R-1: rounded equal EMIs rarely sum to the unrounded total, yet AC-07 demands sum(principal) = disbursed AND sum(principal+interest) = total payable. Where does the rounding residual land?
options: Final installment, total_payable derived from the schedule
decisions.proposed_default: Final installment, total_payable derived from the schedule
decisions.chosen: EMI rounded to 2dp; per-period interest from the opening balance; principal = EMI - interest; the final installment's principal is set to the remaining balance. total_payable is DEFINED as sum(row.principal + row.interest) over the schedule, not EMI x tenure.
decisions.rationale: Deriving total_payable from the stored rows makes both AC-07 invariants true by construction, which is the only way to satisfy them without loosening the invariant test — the failure mode R-1 predicts. Installment count still equals product tenure.

decisions.question: Risk R-2: NFR-02 and NFR-05 forbid update and delete on policy versions and schedules, but FR-10 overrides a decision and FR-09 changes outstanding principal. Where is the immutable/mutable line drawn?
options: Immutable artifacts plus mutable loan state
Fully event-sourced, all state a projection
decisions.proposed_default: Immutable artifacts plus mutable loan state
decisions.chosen: Append-only tables: policy_version, schedule_installment, decision_record, audit_event, repayment_posting. Mutable columns: application.status, loan.outstanding_principal, loan.delinquency_bucket. An FR-10 override appends a new decision_record plus audit_event; an application's current decision is its latest decision_record.
decisions.rationale: Confines the NFR-02/NFR-05 zero-update guarantee to the artifacts the requirements actually name, so the architecture test asserts no UPDATE/DELETE against those five tables only and stops colliding with FR-09 and FR-10. Full event sourcing would turn every read surface (FR-11, FR-12, FR-15) into a projection and put the dashboard's p95 under 500ms at risk.

decisions.question: Risk R-3: FR-13 activates a new policy version with no restart, but FR-04 requires reason codes to exist in the version named on the application. When is the policy version pinned?
decisions.chosen: The application stores policy_version_id at submission; scoring, decision, reason codes, MANUAL_REVIEW re-decisions and any later override all cite that pinned version
decisions.rationale: Pinning at submission is what lets the FR-13 hot-activation test and the FR-04 reason-code test both pass: an activation mid-flight can never change an in-flight application's basis. Pinning at decision time would let two applications submitted together be judged by different rules.

decisions.question: NFR-11 (100% agent-generated, 0 hand-written production lines) is a process constraint, not runnable behavior. How does it enter the story graph?
options: A provenance-check story in the Architecture Invariants epic
decisions.chosen: Governance constraint traced to E16 with no implementation story; evidenced by the standard pre-commit gate set and the /gate attestation record
decisions.rationale: Keeps the NFR-11 trace id alive downstream without inventing a product story the renderer would have to fill with harness plumbing rather than loan-platform behavior.

decisions.question: How should the first stories in each milestone be shaped — vertical tracer bullet, or layer-complete per epic?
options: Tracer bullet per milestone, then depth
decisions.proposed_default: Tracer bullet per milestone, then depth
decisions.chosen: Each milestone opens with one thin end-to-end story reaching its done_when shallowly (M1: login -> catalog -> edit threshold -> new version active; M2: submit -> score -> decide; M3: approve -> disburse -> post repayment), then epics add depth behind it
decisions.rationale: Keeps a runnable, demoable system at every story-group boundary and forces the cross-layer seams (Types through UI) to exist before any epic goes deep, rather than integrating six finished layers late.

decisions.question: Does schedule generation (E9) depend on document verification (E6)?
options: No — only on an APPROVED decision
decisions.proposed_default: No — only on an APPROVED decision
decisions.chosen: No. E9 depends on E5 (a decision of AUTO_APPROVE or an approved MANUAL_REVIEW) only; the E6 -> E9 edge is defensive and is dropped.
decisions.rationale: FR-07 triggers schedule generation on approval and names no document precondition. A real edge here would serialise all of M3 behind the M2 workbench for no requirement.

decisions.question: Does the end-of-day job (E12) depend on repayment posting (E11)?
options: Only on the shared bucket function
decisions.proposed_default: Only on the shared bucket function
decisions.chosen: E12 depends on the bucket-classification function E11 introduces, not on E11's posting endpoint; E12 is built and tested against seeded loans so it can run in parallel with E11's API work
decisions.rationale: AC-14's idempotence assertion needs only loans with due dates and a classifier. Making E12 wait on the posting endpoint is a defensive edge that removes the only parallelism available inside M3.

decisions.question: What does the portfolio dashboard (E14) depend on?
decisions.chosen: E14 is a read model over loan bucket state and overdue installments (E11); no edge to E12
decisions.rationale: AC-15 asserts counts, values and total overdue against stored state, which E11 establishes. The EOD job only refreshes that state on a schedule.

decisions.question: Where does the platform epic (E15) sit in the order?
decisions.chosen: E15 lands first in M1: structured JSON logging, the correlation-id middleware, the log-redaction filter, /health and the Docker Compose stack precede every other epic's first log line
decisions.rationale: NFR-06 asserts 100% of request-scoped log lines carry a correlation id and NFR-03 asserts zero PII occurrences. Both are retrofit-hostile — a later pass would have to revisit every handler written before them. This edge is real, not defensive.

decisions.question: What is the observable criterion for NFR-01 (fixed-point money)?
decisions.chosen: A property test over (principal, rate, tenure) asserts every money field on a generated schedule is a Decimal quantized to exactly 2 decimal places, and a static check reports 0 float arithmetic operations in money code paths (backend decimal.Decimal; frontend integer minor units).
decisions.rationale: NFR-01 stated a target with no observation procedure; spec-render only checks criteria that already exist, so the criterion is authored here.

decisions.question: What is the observable criterion for NFR-02 (policy versions and schedules append-only)?
decisions.chosen: The policy_version and schedule_installment repositories expose no update or delete method (asserted by interface test), and an architecture test reports 0 UPDATE or DELETE statements and 0 ORM mutations against those two tables across src/ and migrations/.
decisions.rationale: Turns NFR-02's zero-update-and-delete target into a check with a stated scope, bounded by the D5 immutable/mutable line.

decisions.question: What is the observable criterion for NFR-03 (no PII in logs)?
decisions.chosen: A test submits an application carrying synthetic PAN, Aadhaar and salary-document content, captures every emitted log record, and asserts 0 occurrences of each value; a second assertion confirms the redaction filter is installed on every configured logger.
decisions.rationale: The capture-and-assert-zero form is what makes NFR-03's zero-occurrence claim observable, and the filter-installation assertion stops a new logger silently bypassing it.

decisions.question: What is the observable criterion for NFR-04 (auth enforced at the controller layer)?
decisions.chosen: For every underwriter and admin route enumerated from the OpenAPI schema, a generated test issues the request with no session (expect 401) and with a CUSTOMER session (expect 403); the test asserts it covered 100% of those routes, so a newly added unguarded route fails the suite.
decisions.rationale: Enumerating from the schema rather than a hand-written list is what delivers NFR-04's 100%-of-routes claim and keeps it true as routes are added.

decisions.question: What is the observable criterion for NFR-05 (append-only migrations)?
decisions.chosen: A migration-lint test parses every file under migrations/ and asserts 0 DROP TABLE, 0 DROP COLUMN and 0 destructive ALTER statements; policy migrations are checked by the same parser.
decisions.rationale: Gives NFR-05's zero-destructive-migrations target a concrete statement set to count, runnable in CI on every commit.

decisions.question: What is the observable criterion for NFR-06 (structured logs with correlation id)?
decisions.chosen: Every log line emitted while serving a request parses as JSON and carries a non-empty request_id equal to the inbound X-Request-ID header, or to a generated id when the header is absent; the assertion covers 100% of request-scoped lines in the captured buffer.
decisions.rationale: Makes NFR-06's 100% countable against a captured buffer instead of a spot check, and fixes header propagation as part of the criterion.

decisions.question: What is the observable criterion for NFR-07 (health endpoint)?
decisions.chosen: In the deploy smoke test, after docker compose up reports the backend healthy, GET /health returns 200 with a JSON body and the measured response time is under 1 second.
decisions.rationale: NFR-07's within-1-second-of-successful-startup needs a defined start point; anchoring it to compose readiness in the smoke test supplies one.

decisions.question: What is the observable criterion for NFR-08 (architecture rules as tests)?
decisions.chosen: An architecture test module holds at least one test per named invariant — policy-version immutability, the EMI principal/rate/tenure invariant, and the one-way dependency rule across Types, Config, Repository, Service, API, UI — and the suite fails if any registered invariant has no corresponding test.
decisions.rationale: NFR-08 names two invariants explicitly and implies the layering rule; the registry-with-no-orphans form makes at-least-one-test-per-invariant enforceable rather than aspirational.

decisions.question: What is the observable criterion for NFR-09 (runtime SLO)?
decisions.chosen: A load run against the read-heavy endpoints (GET /products, GET /applications, GET /loans/{id}, GET /dashboard) reports p95 under 500 ms and an error rate under 1%; the measured figures are recorded in the evaluation report.
decisions.rationale: Names the endpoints the SLO is measured on, so the runtime-SLO sensor has a fixed surface rather than whichever route is convenient.

decisions.question: What is the observable criterion for NFR-10 (WCAG 2.1 AA)?
decisions.chosen: An automated axe-core scan of the Apply, Track and Repay screens reports 0 WCAG 2.1 AA violations, and keyboard-only traversal of each screen's primary flow completes without a focus trap.
decisions.rationale: Pairs an automated zero-violation count with the keyboard check axe cannot see, covering the three screens NFR-10 names.

decisions.question: What is the observable criterion for NFR-11 (agent-generated code)?
decisions.chosen: Governance control rather than a runtime assertion: every production commit on the branch carries agent co-authorship and passes the standard pre-commit gate set, and the /gate attestation record is the evidence for 0 hand-written production lines.
decisions.rationale: Records the observation procedure D7 chose, so NFR-11 keeps a checkable criterion without a product story.

decisions.question: What is the observable criterion for NFR-12 (self-hosted stack and layering)?
decisions.chosen: docker compose up from a clean checkout brings up exactly one Postgres service, the Python 3.12 FastAPI backend and the TypeScript React-Vite frontend, all reporting healthy; the layer-dependency architecture test reports 0 violations of the six-layer one-way rule.
decisions.rationale: Splits NFR-12 into the two things that can actually be observed — a clean-checkout bring-up and a dependency-direction test — instead of leaving it as a stack description.

decisions.question: U1/U2 — the 12 NFRs (NFR-01..NFR-12) were in scope with no BRD acceptance postcondition, so 28 story ACs realizing them registered as net_new and blocked trace-check --layer spec-acceptance. Waive them, or ground them upstream?
options: Record accepts_verdict for the 28 ids on D13-D24 (waiver)
Promote the observation procedures into the source PRD section 6 and re-adopt (upstream evidence)
decisions.proposed_default: Promote the observation procedures into the source PRD section 6 and re-adopt
decisions.chosen: Promoted upstream. The 12 observation procedures from D13-D24 were transcribed into prd/truelend.md section 6 "Acceptance / Done" as NFR-01..NFR-12 rows, then re-extracted with prd-extract.js --tag. brd-acceptance.json went 17 -> 29 criteria; every requirement now carries an acceptance id (NFR acceptance = FRD-57..FRD-68). No accepts_verdict was recorded and no waiver was used — the gate is expected to clear on evidence. Rejected writing brd-acceptance.json directly because the next brd-adopt.js run would erase it.
decisions.rationale: Section 4 of the source PRD already stated each NFR as a measurable postcondition (0 occurrences, p95 under 500 ms, at least 1 test per invariant, 200 within 1 second), so section 6 rows are transcription of existing source content rather than invented oracles. Editing the source keeps adoption verbatim and survives re-adoption, which a hand-written artifact does not. Verified zero drift on FRD-1..FRD-29 ids, labels and the pre-existing FR-01..FR-17 acceptance ids.

decisions.question: U3 — ownership cluster C1 holds 25 of 29 stories at 118 points against a 21-point cap and is biconnected with no bridge to split on. Accept it, or re-shape the edges that close the cycles?
options: Accept C1 as a single-owner cluster and sequence via the 14 waves
Cut the E17-S1 / E15-S3 multi-target fan-in
decisions.proposed_default: Accept C1 as a single-owner cluster and sequence via the 14 waves
decisions.chosen: Accept C1 as a single-owner cluster. One owner takes all 25 stories; sequencing comes from the 14 scheduling waves (A-N), not from cluster-level parallelism. D8 (tracer-first) and D12 (platform-first) stand unchanged, and no recorded edge was removed to silence the warning. The oversize-cluster warning is accepted as a known, recorded condition rather than resolved.
decisions.rationale: C1 is a direct consequence of two deliberate shaping decisions plus honest cross-epic fan-in on E16-S1, E17-S1 and E15-S3 — not a fabricated edge. Dropping D12 would let epics emit their first log lines before logging, correlation and redaction exist, which is the NFR-03/NFR-06 surface; narrowing the E17-S1/E15-S3 fan-in would weaken the very coverage those stories exist to provide. Accepting a sequential build is the cheaper honest trade. Consequence to carry forward: the 4-clusters/14-waves figure must not be presented as cluster parallelism.

decisions.question: U4 — the contract edge E11-S1 -> E12-S1 stopped being a cluster cut because E11-S1 (3 points) fell under the 5-point merge floor and was merged into C2. Does D10 intent still hold?
options: Confirm D10 intent and accept C2 as one 8-point cluster
Re-shape so E11-S1 stays separately startable
decisions.proposed_default: Confirm D10 intent and accept C2 as one 8-point cluster
decisions.chosen: Confirmed. E12-S1 consumes the published delinquency-bucket ladder and schedule data, not E11-S2 posting endpoint, so D10 intent is intact. C2 is owned as a single 8-point cluster and no parallelism is claimed for the cancelled edge.
decisions.rationale: The cancellation is a merge artifact of the undersized-cluster floor, not a dependency error. The edge still carries the correct contract direction; only its status as a cluster cut was lost, and no schedule claim rests on it.

decisions.question: E17-S1 (WCAG) and E15-S3 (SLO) both sat in terminal wave N, fanning in from every screen and read endpoint. D12 front-loaded logging because retrofit is expensive; accessibility and latency have the same property. Move them earlier, or accept terminal verification?
decisions.chosen: Both become early ratchets with registry-enumerated coverage. E17-S1 lands immediately after the first customer screen (E4-S3) and E15-S3 immediately after the first read endpoint (E2-S1). Their fan-in edges are reversed: instead of each depending on every screen/endpoint it measures, the later customer-screen stories (E8-S1 Track, E13-S1 Repay) take a contract edge on E17-S1's harness, and the later read-surface stories (E7-S1, E13-S1, E14-S1) take a contract edge on E15-S3's harness. Both criterion sets are restated in the registry-enumeration form already used by D16 for NFR-04: the check enumerates every registered customer-facing screen / read-heavy endpoint and asserts it covered all of them, so a screen or endpoint added later that violates the budget fails the suite at the story that introduced it.
decisions.rationale: Terminal verification defers the two most retrofit-hostile NFRs past every story that can break them: three customer screens would be built across waves G/I/M with no accessibility signal, then one 5-point story would have to remediate all three, and a p95 miss at wave N would touch every read endpoint. Reversing the fan-in makes the failure attributable to the story that caused it, which is the same reasoning D12 applied to logging, correlation ids and redaction. The registry form keeps FRD-66 and FRD-65 fully asserted — a registry containing Apply, Track and Repay (and the four named read endpoints) satisfies the upstream postcondition and additionally fails closed on an unregistered addition — so no upstream acceptance text changes and no trace id moves. Secondary benefit: removing five fan-in edges retires the cross-epic cycles that U3 named as part of what left C1 without a bridge.
